_comment: Source of truth for the brand-image shortlist. Hand-edit this file, then run ./tools/images-sync.py. Rank is the ORDER within a category — move an entry up to promote it, delete it to drop it. Rebuilt 2026-08-08 as fifty images in six use-led families: each family answers 'which page does this go on', not 'what object is in the picture', because the old split by subject matter put the same photograph in three plausible places. One photographic world throughout: candid over posed, environmental portraits over headshots, humans using technology over technology alone, and real light on real material instead of vector abstracts.

adobe.name: Adobe Stock
adobe.licence: Watermarked comp. Evaluation only until licensed.
adobe.note: Standard subscription. Premium collections (Stocksy, Westend61, peopleimages) are resold here but cost extra.

unsplash.name: Unsplash
unsplash.licence: Unsplash Licence — free for commercial use, no attribution required.
unsplash.note: Free and heavily used, so exclusivity is nil: the same photo can appear on a competitor's site. Good for internal decks and filler; check every frame for third-party logos, which Unsplash does not screen out the way paid libraries do.

envato.name: Envato Elements
envato.licence: Covered by the RBA subscription — licensed on download, usable in production.
envato.note: The only source here that is actually licensed. Previews staged by tools/images-fetch-envato.py are watermarked 1200x630 social crops; download the clean full-size file over the same filename and the watermark goes.

istock.name: iStock
istock.licence: Not licensed. Credit or subscription required before use.
istock.note: Getty's affordable tier. Signature collection is exclusive to Getty/iStock, so it is not resold through Adobe — that is the reason to have it here rather than a price one.

items.title: Diverse coworkers collaborating on open laptop in bright office near windows, woman wearing tan top
items.why: Two colleagues actually reading the same screen, with expressions that belong to the work rather than the camera. Big windows, business casual, no staging.
items.crop: 3:2 as shot; keep both faces and the laptop lid.

items.title: Three colleagues around a laptop with printed charts across the desk, one leaning in over the others
items.why: A desk with a project actually on it — printouts, notebooks, a laptop three people are reading. Everyone is looking at the work rather than past it, which the frame it replaces could not manage.
items.use: Project delivery, team pages, staff augmentation
items.crop: 3:2; keep the printouts in the foreground and the windows behind.

items.title: Two Professionals Review Business Contract Together Before Signing
items.why: Consultant and client at real monitors, one pointing at actual work on screen. Reads as a review, not a photoshoot.
items.crop: Keep both screens; wide crops hold.

items.title: Two colleagues standing in discussion beside a glass wall covered in sticky notes, one holding an open folder
items.why: A standing working conversation with the workshop still on the glass behind it. Gestures and folder do the talking, so it reads as discovery rather than a corridor walk-and-talk.
items.crop: Keep the sticky-note wall in frame; crops to 4:3 without losing either face.

items.title: Two colleagues at one laptop, one holding a printout, working through it together in a bright office
items.why: Someone being shown something — which is what onboarding and internal comms actually look like. Warm daylight, plants, both people in the task rather than posed beside it.
items.crop: 3:2; keep both faces and the printed page.

items.title: I have some ideas for you. Shot of a group of businesspeople having a meeting at work.
items.why: A working session that looks mid-sentence: one person talking, five actually listening, whiteboard scrawl behind. The warm daylight keeps it human.
items.crop: Wide 2:1; crop toward the speaker for cards.

items.title: Business Meeting Between Two Professionals Reviewing Documents on a Tablet in Modern Office Lounge
items.why: Advisor and client on a lounge sofa over one tablet. Financial services warmth without a handshake in sight.
items.crop: 3:2; the sofa's warm palette crops well.

items.title: Wide view of a co-working floor, people working separately across tiered seating and benches
items.why: The establishing shot the library never had — a whole floor, a dozen people, each doing their own work. Every other frame here is one to four people close in; this one says what the place is. Replaces a research-wall photograph shot past a large pink blur.
items.use: About, careers, office and culture pages, section openers
items.crop: Panoramic. Holds a headline in the upper left where the wall is quiet.

items.title: Businesswoman holding digital tablet near whiteboard in meeting
items.why: A whiteboard dense with real writing and a presenter mid-thought. Documentary register that most whiteboard stock never reaches.
items.crop: Keep the whiteboard texture; faces are secondary here.

items.title: Two colleagues working in a glass-walled meeting room, seen through the glass with the office reflected in it
items.why: Observed rather than staged: the frame is taken from outside the room, through glass that carries a green-and-amber reflection of the floor behind. It replaces two people smiling at each other by a window, which was warm and completely generic.
items.crop: 3:2 as shot. The reflection is the picture — do not crop it out to get closer to the faces.

items.title: Four colleagues around a desk with printed documents and monitors, one seated and talking the others through it
items.why: A real working session in a warm, wood-lined office: paper on the desk, screens in use, four people genuinely in the same conversation. Brighter and more contemporary than the dark flip-chart frame it replaces.
items.crop: 3:2; keep the documents in frame. Crops to 16:9 without losing anyone.

items.title: Designer with pink hair working at a laptop in a co-working space, colleagues at work behind
items.why: A real photograph from a premium collection, and a better picture than the generated frame it replaces: a specific person in a specific room, with other people genuinely working behind her. Absorbed in the screen, no eye contact, nothing arranged.
items.use: Capability pages, people pages, article leads
items.crop: 3:2 as shot. Keep the room behind her — it is what makes it an environmental portrait.

items.title: Designer at an iMac in profile, absorbed in the layout on screen, daylight and a plant behind
items.why: A face doing the work, which the frame it replaces did not have — that one was hands over a desk of props. Design shown as concentration rather than as a spread of printed screens.
items.use: UX practice, design services, case studies
items.crop: 3:2; keep the screen content and the window light on his face.

items.title: Man in a blazer reading a document beside an open laptop in a bright, plant-filled office
items.why: Paper and screen in one frame, which is what advisory work actually looks like. Holds the register of the generated image it replaces without the problem: a real room, a real person, a model release that means something.
items.crop: Wide crops hold. Keep the laptop edge and the document both in frame.

items.title: A young woman in a white shirt uses a tablet in a modern office setting with large windows and natural light
items.why: Reading on a tablet, standing at the glass. Quiet, bright, and free of the usual tablet-as-prop stiffness.
items.use: Mobile workflows, reading lists, secondary pages
items.crop: Vertical-friendly; also crops to 3:2.

items.title: Woman graphic designer working at dual monitors in modern office
items.why: Dual monitors, a desk fan, cable clutter: a workstation that is clearly used daily. She turns from the work, not for the camera.
items.crop: Keep both monitors and the room depth.

items.title: Senior executive concentrating on paperwork at a laptop in a glass-walled office
items.why: Replaces a generated image with no model behind it. Brings seniority and range the family was short of, and the concentration is legible without a single gesture aimed at the camera.
items.use: Advisory, leadership, governance, points of view
items.crop: 3:2; keep the documents in frame. Do not crop to a head-and-shoulders portrait.

items.title: Portrait of confident senior woman manager using laptop computer working online sitting in modern office
items.why: A senior manager actually working: laptop, notebook, warm slatted light. Experience without the arms-folded executive pose.
items.crop: 3:2; the blinds pattern rewards a wide crop.

items.title: Man at a laptop at a spare desk, side on, a single lamp and a notebook beside him
items.why: Quiet, unhurried concentration with nothing in the frame that is not being used. Took this slot from a second Marko Geber frame that was the same picture as rank 5 — a woman at a laptop in an open-plan office, same photographer, same family — and it rebalances a set that was five women to three men.
items.crop: 3:2 as shot; the empty desk to his right is where type goes.

items.title: Analyst at a three-monitor desk reaching to a chart on screen in a window-lit office
items.why: Real spreadsheets and real charts across three screens, and a hand reaching into the work. Daylight from the window keeps it out of the blue-glow register the category kept falling into.
items.crop: 3:2; keep at least two screens and the window edge.

items.title: Two colleagues at a monitor in a warm, backlit office, one talking the other through it
items.why: Replaces a frame whose hardware dated it. Same idea, current equipment, better light — and the attention still goes to the screen rather than the lens.
items.crop: 3:2 as shot; keep the window light behind them.

items.title: A briefing under way in a glass-walled room, dashboard on the wall screen, seen from the floor outside
items.why: Observed through the glass rather than staged inside it, so it reads as a meeting that was already happening. Daylight, ordinary clothes, a dashboard nobody is pointing at — the opposite of the neon control room it replaces.
items.crop: 3:2; keep the glass line and the screen. Do not crop into the room.

items.title: Developer at a three-screen workstation with real code open, daylight across a wooden floor
items.why: Actual code on actual screens, headphones over the chair, daylight doing the work. Everything the composited neon-code frame it replaces was pretending to be.
items.crop: 3:2; keep all three displays and the room behind.

items.title: Two analysts at a curved multi-screen desk of live dashboards in a daylit room
items.why: The one frame found in this search that shows analytics without inventing them: real charts on real hardware, two people reading the same thing, daylight rather than a dark operations-centre grade. The generated set could not manage a plottable chart.
items.use: Data and AI service lines, analytics, operations
items.crop: Panoramic. Keep at least three screens legible; crop from the left for 3:2.

items.title: Woman programmer works at desk in modern loft office coding on large monitors with natural light and brick wall
items.why: Code on a big monitor, brick and daylight around it. Engineering that looks like a place you would want to work.
items.crop: 3:2; window flare is part of the appeal.

items.title: Colleague leaning in to explain something on a laptop to a seated coworker, bright office
items.why: Knowledge moving between two people, which is the actual product of a consultancy. Both are engaged with the screen and neither performs for the camera.
items.crop: 3:2 as shot; keep both faces and the laptop.

items.title: Business colleagues reviewing data on tablet at cafe
items.why: A tablet passed across a cafe table between three colleagues. The device sits inside a genuine conversation.
items.crop: Warm tones; crops to square for cards.

items.title: Engineer in a blazer reading a tablet beside a robotic arm on a bright factory floor
items.why: Automation photographed the way rbaconsulting.com photographs industry: business casual, no hard hat, no hi-vis, one person absorbed in a device with the plant soft behind her. The PPE frame it replaces was the furthest thing here from that.
items.crop: 3:2; keep the arm in the foreground blur and her face lit.

items.title: Man in a business shirt checking stock on a tablet in a bright retail aisle
items.why: One person, a device, a real aisle going soft behind — the exact grammar rbaconsulting.com uses for its own photography, and the sharpest retail frame in the set.
items.use: Retail industry page, inventory and store operations
items.crop: 3:2; keep the aisle receding behind him for depth.

items.title: Grower checking a tablet in a ripe cereal field at golden hour
items.why: Agriculture, and the house composition done properly — device in hand, eyes down, the crop and the light doing the rest. A real photograph in place of a generated one, at nearly twice the resolution.
items.crop: Very wide. Crop from either side; keep her below the horizon line.

items.title: Consultant in a blazer and a plant engineer reading a laptop together on a factory floor
items.why: Better than the generated frame it replaces, and not only because it is real: it shows the consulting relationship inside the industry rather than a lone manager. The generated image showed a supervisor in a shirt on a food line — a scene that barely exists, which is part of why it had to be generated.
items.crop: 3:2; keep both figures and the laptop. The plant behind can go.

items.title: Diverse medical team collaborating around a table, discussing healthcare strategies and using laptops
items.why: A clinical team around a table with laptops, glass wall behind. The administrative half of healthcare that photo libraries forget.
items.crop: Wide; crop to the table for cards.

items.title: Adviser and client reading a document together at a desk, warm lamp and glass office behind
items.why: Financial services without the handshake or the boardroom: two people actually reading the same page. Warm, close, believable.
items.crop: 16:9 as supplied — a video-frame asset, so check the pixels against the crop you want.

items.title: Teacher leaning in to help students working at a laptop in a daylit classroom
items.why: Education and the public sector, shown as the work rather than as a building. Real clutter, real attention, nobody looking at the camera.
items.crop: Wide. Crop toward the laptop and the two nearest students for cards.

items.title: Hospital, meeting and doctor with team on tablet for report, patient results and treatment plan
items.why: A doctor mid-explanation, tablet in hand, colleagues leaning in. Clinical teamwork with believable energy.
items.crop: 16:9 native; keep all three faces.

items.title: Four colleagues talking over coffee against a white office wall, one perched on a chair arm
items.why: Four people in an actual conversation, relaxed enough that one of them is half-sitting on a chair. Replaces a frame of two people rummaging in a bag outside a building, which read as looking for keys rather than as anything about working here. The bare wall behind is the most usable quiet area in the family.
items.crop: Very wide. Crop from the left; keep the whole group and the empty wall above them for type.

items.title: Senior colleague guiding a younger one through something on a laptop, bright modern office
items.why: The one thing a careers page needs and this library did not have: somebody teaching somebody else. Both are engaged with the screen, and the seniority reads without a suit.
items.crop: 3:2 as shot; keep both faces and the laptop.

items.title: Diverse coworkers collaborating and talking in a modern office, enjoying a casual break with natural light and plants
items.why: A standing group mid-conversation by the windows, framed through plants. An inclusive group photo that never squares up to the camera.
items.crop: 3:2; keep the foreground greenery.

items.title: Colleagues gathered on a rooftop terrace over the city
items.why: A rooftop table over the city at dusk, string lights up, nobody performing. The informal-social concept where this family lives, outdoors.
items.crop: Wide; the skyline band takes overlay copy.

items.title: Three diverse women laughing with coffee on a city street
items.why: A genuine laugh between three colleagues mid-stride, coffee in hand, on a real street. Humor kept, moved into daylight and the city.
items.crop: 3:2; keep all three faces and the street depth.

items.title: Woman working on a laptop on a sofa in a daylit living room with tall windows
items.why: Wide enough to be about the room, not the laptop. Bright, calm and ungraded, with space at the left for a headline — hybrid work photographed as a life rather than a setup.
items.crop: Wide 3:2; the left third is empty on purpose, so keep it.

items.title: Colleagues talking over coffee at a kitchen counter, more of the office visible through the doorway behind
items.why: A break that reads as a break: cups, a counter, several conversations at once and nobody arranged. Replaces a lunch scene shot between two blurred foreground heads, which is the trope the reject list names.
items.crop: Wide. Keep the doorway and the second group; they are what make it a workplace.

items.title: This is our time to catch up. Shot of two young businessmen walking through the city during their afternoon commute
items.why: Two professionals walking the sunny street, one wheeling a bike. Commute-as-lifestyle with real ease between them.
items.crop: Wide 1.85:1; open sky takes type.

items.title: City grid at dusk from the air, amber streets threading between deep blue blocks
items.why: The closest real photograph to the data-surface this family is now built around: a dark ground, a fine repeating grid, amber against blue, and depth that comes from atmosphere rather than a gradient. An abstract corporate metaphor that happens to be a real place.
items.use: Section headers, hero panels, data and AI pages
items.crop: Panoramic. Reversed white type holds anywhere in the darker blocks.

items.title: Office facade at night, warm lit windows in a dark receding grid
items.why: Repetition, depth and amber-on-dark — the architectural reading of the same idea. Generated, and permitted here: it is a surface with nobody in it, which is the line the library now draws.
items.use: Section headers, quote cards, deck dividers
items.crop: Crop into the darker corner for type. Generated with AI — no people depicted.

items.title: Curved glass office tower at night, floors lit teal behind a sweep of vertical ribs
items.why: Corporate architecture, which the frame it replaces was not — that one was an apartment block, balconies and curtains and all, which is the wrong building for this brand however good the single lit window looked. This has the curve and recess the family lacked, so the depth is structural rather than atmospheric, and it is a photograph rather than a render.
items.use: Section headers, hero panels, About and capability pages
items.crop: Crop into the curve. Reversed white type holds on the darker ribs at either edge.

items.title: Facade of repeating triangular glass panels
items.why: A triangulated facade that reads as a network without a glowing node in sight. Connectivity, drawn by a building.
items.use: Connectivity and platform stories, section breaks
items.crop: Pattern fills any frame; avoid cropping to featurelessness.

items.title: Long-exposure interchange at night, amber and white light trails sweeping across deep navy
items.why: Movement, which every other surface in this family lacks: the same dark ground and amber-against-blue, but drawn as flow rather than grid. Real long-exposure photography, and the darkest quiet areas in the set sit top-left and along the bottom.
items.use: Section headers, hero panels, transformation and delivery pages
items.crop: Panoramic. Reversed white type holds in the dark band above the trails.

items.title: Curved glass towers seen from directly below, converging on a starburst of open sky
items.why: The upward axis the family was missing, and the strongest single piece of corporate-architecture abstraction in it: amber cladding against cool glass, radial rather than rectilinear, real depth. Generated, and permitted — a surface with nobody in it.
items.use: Hero panels, section dividers, About and capability pages
items.crop: Crop toward the centre; the sky aperture is where type wants to sit. Generated with AI — no people depicted.

items.title: Dotted data grid on a dark surface receding into shallow focus, amber and cyan blocks
items.why: The frame this whole family was rebuilt around: a dark ground, fine repeating geometry, amber against cyan, and depth that comes from real focus falloff rather than a gradient. It survived the cut of eight glowing-plexus abstracts precisely because it has that depth — and it is a 3D render, not a photograph, which the rules allow for a surface with nobody in it.
items.use: Data and AI section headers, hero panels
items.crop: Crop into the soft foreground. If type has to sit on the sharp blocks, pick another background.
